Yes, that's exactly the direction — turning a pile of scattered, forgettable links into a library I actually trust and can find my way around.

A couple of things I'd add to make sure we're on the same page, since you captured the spirit well:

When I said tags, I don't just mean sticking labels on — I want it to help me while I type, suggesting tags I've already used so I don't end up with "recipe" and "recipes" and "cooking" all meaning the same thing. And searching should feel smart: I want to be able to search by a tag specifically, and combine things — like "show me anything about Rome that's either an article or a book" — not just type one word and hope.

On the reading side, "read later" is one thing, but I also picture the list itself being pleasant to skim — I should see the title, the description, and the tags right there, and clicking an item should just take me to the actual page.

And the whole thing is just for me — my own personal home base. I'm not thinking about other people logging in or sharing.

Does that all still fit what you're picturing?
